title: What became of Freddie's cornet; Keppard's own lessons
summary: Keppard holds Freddie's first little cornet; Herb Moran bought the later one from Freddie's wife. Keppard himself got cornet lessons from Mal Perez and Hippolyte Charles.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Well, I got his little cornet now. You don't have it now? No. He went to Chicago with the cornet and then he bought a new cornet. And this fellow here, just remember what he was for, he's dead now. But he's lived.
Well, then, then, Herb Moran maybe had it right?

Well, Moran is the one, excuse me, Moran is the one that bought his cornet. Because when he came down here before he died, he told me that Fred is cornet, when Fred died, he bought it from Sadie or his wife up there. And he's been having it and playing down here with it. And he showed it to me. Of course, nevertheless, I was fooling cornet myself a little bit because Mal Perez would give me ideas and he'd give me a lesson. And also Hippolyte Shaw would give me lessons. But that was the music lessons only. And you see, at those times when I was coming up, well, they couldn't pick up no interpreter. You'd have to beat the value of the time before you pick up an instrument.
